figures.finding: Western Australian law is in force in the Cocos (Keeling) Islands (Cocos (Keeling) Islands Act 1955 s. 8A, unless an Ordinance suspends it; none was looked for), and under it a person attains full age and full capacity at eighteen; no WA statute read sets aside a child performer's earnings, and none distinguishes writing or directing.

value.follows: AU (Western Australia's laws, applied by the Cocos (Keeling) Islands Act 1955 s. 8A; Commonwealth Acts that extend to the Territory)

figures.applies: Cocos (Keeling) Islands Act 1955 s. 8A; WA Age of Majority Act 1972 s. 5 (as read for AU, 2026-11-01). How WA binds a minor's contract was not found (AU's blocker).

sources.said: 8A Application of Western Australian laws (1) Subject to this section, section 8G and Part IVAA, Western Australian laws are in force in the Territory. ... (3) An Ordinance may suspend the operation in the Territory of a law in force in the Territory under subsection (1) for such period as is specified in the Ordinance.
(a)a person who, on or after the commencing day, attains the age of 18 years attains full age and full capacity on attaining that age;

figures.finding: Under Western Australia's Children and Community Services Act 2004, applied in the Territory, no one may employ a child under fifteen in a business, trade or occupation carried on for profit, but the bar doesn't apply to a child employed in a dramatic or musical performance or other entertainment or in making an advertisement: no permit, no hours rule; employing a child to perform indecently is a crime, and the Department's CEO may prohibit or limit a child's employment. The exception names performance and advertising only (reading: a child employed to write or direct for profit falls under the bar below fifteen).

figures.finding: Only an individual of at least eighteen may be appointed a director of a company under the Corporations Act 2001, whose 'Territory' includes the Territory of Cocos (Keeling) Islands.
